title: Robustifying Vision-Language Models via Test-Time Prompt Adaptation
claim: Single corrupted inputs lose class structure, but distributions of augmented views retain it, enabling distribution-level alignment that improves robustness.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid; scatter plots with zoom-in dashed callouts, bar chart
description: Four-panel figure. Panel (a), top left, shows a stack of adversarially perturbed cheetah images with a red box on the animal. A dashed zoom callout leads to a t-SNE scatter of many small, mixed-color points with no clear class clusters. Panel (b), bottom left, shows a stack of augmented crops of the same adversarial image in red frames. A callout leads to a t-SNE scatter of tight, well-separated colored clusters. Panel (c), top right, is a schematic. Stacked images feed a blue Gaussian bump into an oval labeled Alignment. A green Gaussian above, labeled Prompt with a flame icon, and a pink Gaussian below connect to the oval with arrows. A dotted red arrow leads from the image to a Cache Updating box. Panel (d), bottom right, is a grouped bar chart of accuracy for RN50, ViT-B/32 and ViT-B/16. CLIP under attack is near zero, while CLIP clean and Ours under attack are both around 45 to 53. The eye goes first to the contrast between the scatter plots in (a) and (b).
caption: Augmented views retain more semantic cues under adversarial perturbations, enabeling a cache for distribution alignment that improves adversarial performance. (a) Visualization of adversarially perturbed images, where each point represents an image and different colors denote ground-truth classes. (b) Visualization of multiple augmented views generated from the same adversarial image, colored by class label, where semantic structure partially re-emerges with improved class separability compared to (a). (c) Our method leverages the selected augmented views as a cache and aligns them with textual prompts. (d) Performance comparison across different VLM backbones, demonstrating improved robustness under adversarial attacks.
abstract: Pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as CLIP achieve strong zero-shot generalization, but their performance degrades sharply under adversarial perturbations. Existing test-time adaptation methods typically rely on sample-level confidence heuristics, overlooking the intrinsic distributional structure of the data. This sample-centric approach limits robustness, as it fails to distinguish confident adversarial mispredictions from true semantic consistency. In this work, we observe that adversarial distortion is structurally brittle: while holistic representations are corrupted, semantic integrity is often preserved in the distribution of augmented views. Motivated by this insight, we propose RITA, a Robust test-tIme prompt-TAdaptation framework that shifts from sample-level estimates to distribution-level alignment. Specifically, RITA employs optimal transport to align the distribution of augmented visual features with textual prototypes, mitigating adversarial outliers and rectifying cross-modal semantic misalignment. Furthermore, we introduce a dynamic cache to progressively accumulate reliable cues from the test stream for online refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RITA significantly improves adversarial robustness without compromising clean accuracy.
